# ramabana


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

> rama's arrow. a harness that does not miss.

ramabana is the *brain* of a coding agent, and nothing else. It has no editor, no
frontend and no opinion about where it is running: everything it needs from the
application around it arrives through one protocol, `Host`, and everything it needs
from a model arrives through [rishi](https://github.com/vedicreader/rishi).

It grew up inside [leela](https://github.com/vedicreader/leela), where it was written
against that seam from the first commit — nothing in it ever imported the IDE — and now
stands on its own, with leela as its first consumer.

## The layering

```
rishi      the engine    Chat over litert / llama.cpp / MLX / hosted, and the tool loop
  ↑
ramabana   the harness   Host, tools, approval, routing, compaction, skills, sub-agents
  ↑
leela      the app       folders, notebooks, kernels, two frontends
```

Each arrow points at a dependency, and there are no arrows back. rishi does not know
ramabana exists; ramabana does not know leela exists.

## What is in it

| | |
|---|---|
| `host` | what an application must supply to host an agent |
| `backend` | one chat protocol, over a local model and a hosted one |
| `models` | the model table, and which model each *job* runs on |
| `hitl` | approval as a conversation, with the reason carried back |
| `compact` | surviving a long conversation, and saying so afterwards |
| `skills` | skills discovered from installed packages and `SKILL.md` dirs |
| `activity` | the live account of what the agent is doing |
| `native` | catching what a native engine prints instead of raising |
| `tools` | the tools, written against `Host` |
| `extensions` | user python that registers more of all of the above |
| `subagent` | delegation to a cheap model whose context is thrown away |
| `chat` | the facade the application holds |
| `testing` | a host and a backend with nothing behind either |

## Install

``` sh
pip install ramabana
```

## Use

An agent needs a host. The smallest real one is a dict:

``` python
from ramabana import Agent
from ramabana.testing import MemHost

a = Agent(MemHost({'/proj/a.py': 'x = 1\n'}))
print(a.ask('what is in a.py?'))
```

Anything the host cannot do is not offered to the model as a tool, so a partially-built
host gives a smaller agent rather than a broken one. `host.py` is the whole specification,
and its docstrings are the contract — a host that satisfies the signatures and not the
contracts is a host that quietly hands an agent the whole filesystem.

## Routing

The routing key is the **job**, not the conversation. Pointing the turn at a frontier
model must not drag the completions along with it:

| job | goes to |
|---|---|
| `turn` | whatever you configured; this is the work |
| `completion` | local, always. Fires constantly, must feel instant |
| `classify` | local, always. One label out; a frontier model is pure waste |
| `summary` | local by default. It reads a transcript already in hand |
| `subagent` | local by default. Fan-out burns tool results, not reasoning |

`$RAMABANA_MODEL` sets the turn; `$RAMABANA_MODEL_SUMMARY` and friends move one job.
The `$LEELA_*` spellings are still read, so an existing leela setup keeps working.

## Develop

The notebooks in `nbs/` are the source; `ramabana/*.py` is generated from them. Each
notebook ends with a `## Tests` section that runs against the module it just built, so
opening one and running it shows the behaviour rather than just a green bar.

``` sh
pip install -e '.[dev]'
nbdev_prepare      # export, test, and clean
```
